sections.title: OVERNIGHT MAP
sections.content:
Risk appetite held through Thursday's US session as mega-cap tech continued to carry the tape. S&P 500 closed near session highs, with MSFT and TSLA the day's biggest drivers. Bond yields pulled back modestly, providing a tailwind for growth names. The AI narrative remains the dominant force — MSFT's continued strength reflects confidence in the Copilot monetization path. Tariff concerns haven't fully receded but are no longer the primary intraday catalyst, with markets bifurcating between AI winners and everything else.

3 anchor numbers: SPY +0.79% | 10-yr yield -4bps to ~4.52% | HSI +0.82%

sections.title: US CLOSE MOVERS
sections.content:
Top 3:
- TSLA +7.62% — largest single-name move; sentiment-driven rebound, no new fundamental catalyst
- NET +6.43% — insider-selling headline triggered short-term covering; thesis still under review per portfolio note
- MSFT +4.61% — strong AI integration momentum; Azure growth narrative intact

Bottom 3:
- MU -2.03% — memory sector under pressure; HBM supply concerns creating headwinds
- ETN -1.70% — industrial/electrical equipment soft; cyclical growth concerns persist
- DXYZ -1.20% — speculative punt, no news; tape remains hostile to unprofitable risk

sections.title: HK LIVE MOVERS
sections.content:

- GDS -0.74% — data center name soft; MU weakness likely weighing on semis sentiment

sections.title: MARKET NEWS
sections.content:
1. Trump administration signals tariff escalation — fresh threats against additional Chinese goodskeep the trade war overhang alive. Markets are pricing a 60-70% probability of further tariff announcements before mid-year. Semis and China-adjacent names remain the most exposed.

2. Fed minutes released — policymakers remain data-dependent and cautious on rate cuts, citing sticky services inflation and labor market resilience. Markets pushed back rate-cut expectations slightly; no new easing signal. The "higher for longer" message is intact.

sections.title: ACTION BOARD
sections.content:
• Opportunity: MSFT at +4.61% with AI momentum — hold and let run rather than trim. Copilot monetization is the clearest near-term growth driver among mega-caps.

• Risk: MU continuing to lag — -2.03% today compounds the weak trend. HBM supply headwinds may persist; do not average into weakness without a clear catalyst resolution.

• Research: TSLA +7.62% rebound — per portfolio rules, predefine the trim level. A legacy bag can become dominant risk fast. Review the scenario matrix rule on TSLA-specific squeezes before getting emotionally attached to the move.
